source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Keep gowns and gloves at a distant central station and enter the room first, then return for PPE only if direct contact with the client becomes necessary.","B":"Wear gloves only after visible contamination occurs, because Contact Precautions do not require PPE before touching the client or nearby environment.","C":"Put on the gown after completing care and leave it on while moving to the next room, because the same protective garment can be used between clients.","D":"Make gown and gloves readily accessible nearby at the point of use and don the indicated PPE before contact with the client or contaminated environment."}}
source_row.rationale: For Contact Precautions, gown and gloves should be readily available so indicated PPE can be donned before contact with the patient or the patient's potentially contaminated environment. PPE is removed appropriately after care and is not worn from one patient's environment to another.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Isolation Precautions recommendations V.B.3.a-b: for Contact Precautions, don gown and gloves upon entry into the room/cubicle and remove before leaving the patient-care environment. Current CDC isolation recommendations reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Isolation Precautions, PPE Accessibility Standards
source_row.stem: A nurse prepares to enter the room of a client on Contact Precautions. Which PPE practice is most appropriate?
